C
A projection is a way of representing a three-dimensional object on a two-dimensional surface, similar to how light casts a shadow of an object onto a flat plane. This is fundamental to creating technical drawings like top, front, and side views.

B
A sphere is a 3D object where every point on its surface is an equal distance (the radius) from its center.

C
This is the standard formula for the surface area of a sphere. The other options represent the area of a circle (A), the circumference of a circle (B), and the volume of a sphere (D).

B
The shadow cast by a sphere onto a flat surface is a circle with the same radius, r, as the sphere. The area of a circle is calculated by the formula A = πr².

C
The surface area of a sphere is 4πr², while the area of its projected shadow (a circle) is πr². Thus, the surface area is four times the shadow area.
